newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via multi-day system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via multi-day system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to inject reserves into the banking system through a round of multi-day system repurchase agreements Monday, analysts said.
Seven-day system RPs are most likely, but three-day RPs are possible, they said.
The Fed faces around a $12.5 billion add need for the first week of the maintenance period, which ends Wednesday. But two 14-day system RPs are outstanding, giving the Fed some breathing room.
Fed funds were trading at the 5-1/4 percent target rate.
James Blumenthal, money market economist at MCM MoneyWatch, noted that while seven-day system RPs are most likely, three-day system RPs cannot be ruled out.

"Since one of the 14-day fixed fixed system RPs runs off Thursday, a seven-day operation that would still be in place on Thursday would leave the Fed with less to do in a thin market than if it executed a three-day system RPs today that would also run off on Thursday," he said.
